title: Prediction: a superconducting toggle leaves a residual Casimir torque

statements.text: In a torsion-balance Casimir apparatus, switching a plate through its superconducting transition leaves a state-correlated residual torque after the standard Casimir null model and nuisances are subtracted, measuring the dimensionless product $\eta_1 \Delta\gamma_t$.
statements.falsification_criteria: No residual differential signal remains after standard modeling and nuisance subtraction, which bounds $|\eta_1 \Delta\gamma_t|$ at the achieved torque sensitivity, usually at 95 percent confidence.

prediction.resolution_criterion: A torsion-balance Casimir measurement across a superconducting transition reports a nonzero state-correlated residual $\eta_1 \Delta\gamma_t$ that survives the null checks, or an upper bound on it.

sources.quote: The resulting observable is the dimensionless product η1 ∆γt , extracted from differential torque measurements across the superconducting transition.
It need not be advertised as a refutation of the entire framework, but it does exclude part of its experimentally accessible parameter space and thereby sharpens the theory.
